title: Long exact sequence of the right derived functors of a left exact functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives and $\mathcal B$ an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor and $R^nv$ ($n\geq0$) its right derived functors, computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive], [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ in $\mathcal A$ there are morphisms $\delta^n:R^nv(C)\to R^{n+1}v(A)$ ($n\geq0$) such that the sequence $0\to R^0v(A)\xrightarrow{R^0v(f)}R^0v(B)\xrightarrow{R^0v(g)}R^0v(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}R^1v(A)\to\cdots\to R^nv(A)\xrightarrow{R^nv(f)}R^nv(B)\xrightarrow{R^nv(g)}R^nv(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^n}R^{n+1}v(A)\to\cdots$ is exact.

source.place: Lemma Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), part (1) for complexes concentrated in degree 0, with part (2) for the start of the sequence; classically: horseshoe lemma (an injective resolution of B compatible with given resolutions of A and C, degreewise split) and the long exact cohomology sequence of the resulting short exact sequence of complexes v(I_A) -> v(I_B) -> v(I_C)

proof.text: **Step 1 (resolutions of the short exact sequence).** By the horseshoe lemma [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses] applied to $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ there are injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $s_A:A\to I_A^\bullet$, $s_B:B\to I_B^\bullet$, $s_C:C\to I_C^\bullet$, all zero in negative degrees, and morphisms of complexes $\alpha:I_A^\bullet\to I_B^\bullet$, $\beta:I_B^\bullet\to I_C^\bullet$ with $\alpha^0s_A=s_Bf$, $\beta^0s_B=s_Cg$, such that $0\to I_A^n\xrightarrow{\alpha^n}I_B^n\xrightarrow{\beta^n}I_C^n\to0$ is short exact for every $n\geq0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T (lemma-injective-resolution-ses), parts (2)-(3), for the complexes A[0] -> B[0] -> C[0]

proof.text: **Step 2 (the sequences are split in each degree, so $v$ keeps them exact).** Fix $n\geq0$. Since $\alpha^n$ is a monomorphism and $I_A^n$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the identity of $I_A^n$ extends along $\alpha^n$: there is $r:I_B^n\to I_A^n$ with $r\alpha^n=\mathrm{id}$. The endomorphism $e=\mathrm{id}-\alpha^nr$ of $I_B^n$ satisfies $e\alpha^n=0$; since $\beta^n$ is a cokernel of $\alpha^n$ (exactness at $I_B^n$ and $I_C^n$), $e=\sigma\beta^n$ for a unique $\sigma:I_C^n\to I_B^n$, and $\beta^n\sigma\beta^n=\beta^ne=\beta^n$ with $\beta^n$ epi gives $\beta^n\sigma=\mathrm{id}$. So $r\alpha^n=\mathrm{id}$, $\beta^n\sigma=\mathrm{id}$, $\beta^n\alpha^n=0$, $\alpha^nr+\sigma\beta^n=\mathrm{id}$. The functor $v$ is additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], so it preserves composition, identities, zero morphisms and sums of morphisms; hence the same four identities hold for $v(\alpha^n),v(\beta^n),v(r),v(\sigma)$. These identities make $0\to v(I_A^n)\to v(I_B^n)\to v(I_C^n)\to0$ short exact in the abelian category $\mathcal B$ [def-sp-abelian]: $v(\alpha^n)$ is a split mono, $v(\beta^n)$ a split epi, and if $x$ is killed by $v(\beta^n)$ then $x=v(\alpha^n)v(r)x+v(\sigma)v(\beta^n)x=v(\alpha^n)(v(r)x)$, so the kernel of $v(\beta^n)$ is the image of $v(\alpha^n)$ (in element-free form: $\mathrm{id}-v(\alpha^n)v(r)=v(\sigma)v(\beta^n)$ vanishes on $\ker v(\beta^n)$). Thus $0\to v(I_A^\bullet)\xrightarrow{v(\alpha)}v(I_B^\bullet)\xrightarrow{v(\beta)}v(I_C^\bullet)\to0$, where $v$ is applied termwise and $v(\alpha),v(\beta)$ are morphisms of complexes because $v$ preserves composition, is short exact in each degree. (Only additivity of $v$ is used here; in Mathlib: ShortComplex.ShortExact.splittingOfInjective, ShortComplex.Splitting.map, ShortComplex.Splitting.shortExact.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0136 (lemma-characterize-injectives), (1) => (3): a short exact sequence 0 -> I -> A -> B -> 0 with I injective splits; used in derived.tex Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 1 ('the lower short exact sequence is termwise split')

proof.text: **Step 3 (long exact cohomology sequence).** Put $K_1=v(I_A^\bullet)$, $K_2=v(I_B^\bullet)$, $K_3=v(I_C^\bullet)$: cochain complexes of $\mathcal B$ indexed by $\mathbf N$ (zero in negative degrees), with the degreewise short exact sequence $0\to K_1\xrightarrow{v(\alpha)}K_2\xrightarrow{v(\beta)}K_3\to0$ of Step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] there are morphisms $\partial^n:H^n(K_3)\to H^{n+1}(K_1)$, $n\geq0$, such that $H^0(K_1)\to H^0(K_2)\to H^0(K_3)\xrightarrow{\partial^0}H^1(K_1)\to\cdots\to H^n(K_2)\to H^n(K_3)\xrightarrow{\partial^n}H^{n+1}(K_1)\xrightarrow{H^{n+1}(v\alpha)}H^{n+1}(K_2)\to\cdots$ is exact at every term after the first.

**Step 4 (the start: $H^0(v\alpha)$ is a monomorphism).** Since $K_i^{-1}=0$, $H^0(K_i)=\ker(d^0:K_i^0\to K_i^1)$ and $H^0(v\alpha)$ is the restriction of $v(\alpha^0):K_1^0\to K_2^0$ to these kernels, i.e. $H^0(v\alpha)$ composed with the inclusion $H^0(K_2)\hookrightarrow K_2^0$ equals $v(\alpha^0)$ composed with the inclusion $H^0(K_1)\hookrightarrow K_1^0$. The latter composite is a monomorphism ($v(\alpha^0)$ is a split mono by Step 2), hence so is $H^0(v\alpha)$. So $0\to H^0(K_1)\to H^0(K_2)$ is exact, and the whole sequence of Step 3, preceded by $0$, is exact.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain), for complexes vanishing in negative degrees (H^{-1}(K_3)=0)

proof.text: **Step 5 (identification with $R^nv$).** By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] there are isomorphisms $\iota_A^n:R^nv(A)\to H^n(K_1)$, $\iota_B^n:R^nv(B)\to H^n(K_2)$, $\iota_C^n:R^nv(C)\to H^n(K_3)$ for the resolutions $I_A^\bullet,I_B^\bullet,I_C^\bullet$ of Step 1, and, because $\alpha$ lifts $f$ ($\alpha^0s_A=s_Bf$) and $\beta$ lifts $g$ ($\beta^0s_B=s_Cg$), $R^nv(f)=(\iota_B^n)^{-1}H^n(v\alpha)\iota_A^n$ and $R^nv(g)=(\iota_C^n)^{-1}H^n(v\beta)\iota_B^n$. Define $\delta^n:=(\iota_A^{n+1})^{-1}\circ\partial^n\circ\iota_C^n:R^nv(C)\to R^{n+1}v(A)$. Then the isomorphisms $\iota^n_\bullet$ form an isomorphism from the sequence $0\to R^0v(A)\xrightarrow{R^0v(f)}R^0v(B)\xrightarrow{R^0v(g)}R^0v(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}R^1v(A)\to\cdots$ of the statement to the exact sequence of Steps 3-4 (every square commutes by the two displayed identities and the definition of $\delta^n$). Exactness at a term is preserved under such an isomorphism of sequences (kernels and images correspond under the vertical isomorphisms), so the sequence of the statement is exact. (The statement is about $R^0v$; its identification $R^0v\cong v$ is a separate result used by the citers, not here. Left exactness of $v$ is not used in this proof.)

lean.statement: theorem exists_rightDerived_full_long_exact {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} A] [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian A] [EnoughInjectives A] [Abelian B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] {S : ShortComplex A} (hS : S.ShortExact) : ∃ δ : ∀ n : ℕ, (F.rightDerived n).obj S.X₃ ⟶ (F.rightDerived (n + 1)).obj S.X₁, Mono ((F.rightDerived 0).map S.f) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (S.map (F.rightDerived n)).Exact ∧ ∃ (w₁ : (F.rightDerived n).map S.g ≫ δ n = 0) (w₂ : δ n ≫ (F.rightDerived (n + 1)).map S.f = 0), (ShortComplex.mk _ _ w₁).Exact ∧ (ShortComplex.mk _ _ w₂).Exact
